methods.label: Marginal probabilities and linearity of expectation
methods.explanation: Each of the two draws has marginal probability \(3/6\) of being in the category. By linearity of expectation, \(E[X]=2\times(3/6)=1\). Independence of the draws is not required.
methods.levelReason: Uses finite 0-or-1 draw contributions and addition of their expectations, within the high-school elective probability scope.

candidate.annotationRationale:
The task-level target is the hypergeometric category-count mean, cnm_h258. The actual retained route uses the mean of each 0-or-1 contribution, covered by cnm_h251, with equally likely marginal probabilities supported by cnm_285 and expectation meaning supported by cnm_h252. General finite linearity is missing from the catalog and is proposed separately; the method does not assume independent draws.

needsNewNodes.name: Linearity of expectation for finite sums
needsNewNodes.description: For finitely many finite-valued random variables, the expectation of their sum equals the sum of their expectations, without requiring independence. Apply this to counts expressed as sums of 0-or-1 contributions.
needsNewNodes.reason: The retained method explicitly relies on finite linearity. cnm_h252 covers expectation as a probability-weighted mean, and cnm_h251 covers one 0-or-1 variable, but neither explicitly covers addition of dependent random variables' expectations.
